pr_title: Feature(pr-sum): add --local capture of the checked-out branch
verdict: READY TO MERGE - 10 of 10 findings resolved, 0 bubbled
strengths: Every new test drives real git in a throwaway clone; the only stub is gh_metadata, a collaborator, so no mock-chain wiring tests.
test_diff_refuses_after_a_branch_switch pins the branch half of the moved-checkout guard by switching from detached HEAD to the PR branch at the same SHA.
test_skeleton_without_local_branch_diffs_on_the_pr_branch covers the old-skeleton fallback (local_branch absent reads as the PR head branch) in both the accept and refuse directions.
test_untracked_only_checkout_records_no_working_tree checks that untracked=False also drops working_tree to False, and contrasts it with the untracked-keeping capture.
The render parametrization in test_pr_summary.py covers all four _checkout_label branches (other branch, detached, same as head, None).
The CLI tests exercise the --local/--remote-head mutual exclusion and the --local + --committed-only combination through main().
local_branch defaults to None, so old skeletons still load: facts_from_payload and _require_captured_checkout read them as the PR branch.
A detached HEAD records '' (current_branch's empty string), and None means 'PR branch', so the two never collide in the checkout guard or the Source label.
lacks_pr_head separates git exit 1 (provably lacks the head) from a missing object, so --no-fetch never produces a false warning.
A mutually exclusive argparse group enforces that --local and --remote-head cannot be combined, so no runtime check is needed.
_source_typed validates the new field's type before a skeleton is trusted.
The argument-hint, the capture command and the pr_sum.py usage docstring list the same flags, with --local and --remote-head as mutually exclusive, matching the argparse group.
--repo DIR is added to the diff and build commands as well as capture, so a capture under another project does not lead to a diff or build against the wrong project's skeleton.
The note: text, detached-HEAD caveat and carry-forward rule for descriptions match _local_note, lacks_pr_head and the previous_draft behavior.
local_branch defaults to None and old skeletons read as the PR branch, so earlier payloads still diff; test_skeleton_without_local_branch_diffs_on_the_pr_branch covers that path.

_require_captured_checkout compares against the captured branch, an empty string for a detached HEAD, so `diff` refuses a branch switch after a --local capture; the detached-HEAD limitation is stated in both the script docstring and the SKILL.
lacks_pr_head separates git exit 1 (provably missing) from 128 (object unknown), so --no-fetch without the PR head object never prints a false note.
--local and --remote-head sit in an argparse mutually exclusive group, and the SKILL tells the agent to reject the pair, so the two layers agree.

The new tests are behavioral against real git clones: staged, unstaged and untracked splits, stacked commits, detached HEAD, --committed-only and the PR-head note all exercise real capture logic, with only gh faked.
The version bump, argument-hint, usage block, --help text, README row and SKILL all describe the same flag set, and --repo is threaded through diff and build in the SKILL.

important.name: --local from a checkout lacking the PR head silently drops drafted descriptions
important.summary:
_cmd_capture overwrites the default skeleton (<summaries>/<NNNN>_pr.json) and carry_draft keeps descriptions only for facts.described, so a --local capture from a checkout without the PR head discards every description written for PR files that checkout lacks. The default capture never reads such a checkout, so this loss is new with --local. _local_note fires only after the write and says only that PR files are missing; it says nothing about lost descriptions. Its docstring says 'a rerun drops descriptions', but this same capture already dropped them.

Also (overall): _cmd_capture passes untracked=not args.local unconditionally, so `capture --local` run while the PR branch itself is checked out leaves out untracked files that the default capture keeps (new modules not yet `git add`-ed vanish from the summary). The header still reads `local branch at ..., plus uncommitted changes`, identical to a default capture. SKILL.md:66-70 and README.md:19 present --local as covering a checkout other than the PR branch, which implies it changes nothing on the PR branch. TestCaptureForcedLocal.test_on_the_pr_branch_matches_the_default (tests/scripts/test_pr_sum.py:470) asserts forced == default, but the pr_repo fixture has no untracked file, so it passes only because nothing differs; add one untracked file and the assertion fails.
fix: In _cmd_capture, compute the previous draft's non-empty descriptions whose paths are absent from the fresh facts.described, and name their count in the --local note (e.g. '; N drafted descriptions dropped'). Correct the _local_note docstring to say this capture drops them.
Refuse a --local capture whose HEAD lacks the PR head when it would overwrite an existing draft with non-empty descriptions, unless --out names a different file.

Drop untracked files only off the PR branch: in capture_pr, keep untracked files when _on_pr_branch(repo, meta) holds (for example `untracked or _on_pr_branch(...)`), and add an untracked file to test_on_the_pr_branch_matches_the_default so the equality covers it.

Keep the behavior but document it: state in SKILL.md, README.md and the pr_sum.py docstring that --local leaves untracked files out on the PR branch as well, and rewrite test_on_the_pr_branch_matches_the_default to write an untracked file and assert that it is missing from the forced capture.

important.name: Digits-only value rule now rejects the --repo DIR path
important.summary: Step 1 adds `--repo DIR` to the flags the skill passes through, but the next sentence still reads "Any other flag, a value holding anything but digits, ... is a problem to report; stop." A `--repo` value is a path such as `E:/proj`, which holds non-digits, so an agent that follows the rule as written stops on every `--repo` invocation that the same paragraph says to pass through. Before this PR every value-taking flag (`--level`, `--min-viz`) took digits, so the rule held. Now it contradicts the flag list and the capture command on line 57.
fix: Limit the digits rule to the numeric flags, e.g. "Any other flag, a `--level` or `--min-viz` value holding anything but digits, or `--local` together with `--remote-head` is a problem to report; stop."

minor.name: README says --local works 'the same way', then lists a difference
minor.summary: The pr-sum row says `--local` covers any other branch checkout "the same way (commits since the PR base plus staged and unstaged changes, no untracked files)". The PR-branch capture just described includes untracked files, so "the same way" contradicts the parenthetical that follows it.
fix: Drop "the same way": "`--local` covers any other branch checkout (commits since the PR base plus staged and unstaged changes, no untracked files)".

minor.name: pr_capture module docstring still says only the PR branch is read locally
minor.summary: The module docstring says capture_pr 'on request it reads the local PR branch's HEAD and working tree in place of the committed PR head'. capture_pr now also reads any checked-out branch or a detached HEAD (force_local), with untracked files optionally left out.
fix: Extend the sentence: '...reads the local PR branch's HEAD and working tree (or, with force_local, whatever is checked out) in place of the committed PR head'.

minor.name: PrFacts docstring limits head_source local to the PR branch
minor.summary:
The PrFacts docstring says head_source is 'local when it is the checked-out PR branch's HEAD' and that working_tree adds 'that checkout's uncommitted and untracked changes'. With force_local, head_source is local for any branch or a detached HEAD, and --local leaves untracked files out.

Also (overall): The PrFacts docstring (pr_summary.py:70-71) says head_source `local` means head_sha is 'the checked-out PR branch's HEAD', and the pr_capture module docstring (pr_capture.py:5-6) says capture_pr 'reads the local PR branch's HEAD and working tree'. With force_local, a local capture can now be any branch or a detached HEAD, which the new local_branch field records.
fix: Reword to: '``local`` when it is the checked-out HEAD (the PR branch, or any checkout under ``--local``); ``working_tree`` adds that checkout's uncommitted changes (untracked files too, unless the capture left them out).'
pr_summary.py:70-71: say `local` when it is the checkout's HEAD (the PR branch, or any checkout under force_local). pr_capture.py:5-6: add 'or, with force_local, whatever is checked out'.

minor.name: Source label calls a stale same-name branch the PR branch
minor.summary:
_checkout_label returns 'local branch' whenever local_branch equals facts.head. Under --local, a stale local branch with the PR head's name, one that _on_pr_branch rejects because it lacks the PR head, still gets the PR-branch label. The saved summary then gives no sign that it describes a checkout without the PR head. The CLI note warns only on the console.

Also (overall): _checkout_label returns `local branch` whenever local_branch equals facts.head. Under --local, a stale or unrelated branch carrying the PR head's name (one that does not contain the PR head) gets the same `**Source:** local branch` line as a real PR-branch capture. SKILL.md:64 counts such a branch as 'elsewhere', and SKILL.md:70 promises `local checkout` for a --local capture off the PR branch. A detached capture renders `local detached checkout`, which the SKILL wording does not mention either. Only the transient capture-line note marks the stale case, and the built summary loses it.
fix: Record whether HEAD contains the PR head in PrFacts (e.g. a bool set from _on_pr_branch at capture), and use 'local branch' only when it does. Otherwise use 'local checkout `<name>`'.

Record in capture_pr whether the PR-branch test (_on_pr_branch) held, for example by storing local_branch as the PR branch name only when it held, and let _checkout_label use that, so a stale same-named branch renders as `local checkout `<name>``.
Reword SKILL.md:70 to say the label keys on the branch name (a same-named stale branch reads `local branch`, a detached HEAD `local detached checkout`).

minor.name: --local on the PR branch silently drops untracked files
minor.summary:
SKILL.md describes `--local` only for a checkout that is not the PR branch, and says the PR branch capture includes untracked files. `_cmd_capture` passes `untracked=not args.local` (plugins/harness/scripts/pr_sum.py:384) whatever is checked out, and `_head` takes the local HEAD on the PR branch as well. So `--local` run on the PR branch leaves untracked files out, while the Source line still reads `local branch ..., plus uncommitted changes`. A developer who asks for `--local` on the PR branch gets less than the default capture, and the docs do not mention it.

Also (docs): SKILL.md says a `--local` capture off the PR branch adds a Source line reading `local checkout`. `_checkout_label` (plugins/harness/lib/harness_lib/pr_summary.py:404-408) emits ``local checkout `<branch>` `` for a named branch and `local detached checkout` for a detached HEAD. The skill even mentions the detached case in the same paragraph. An agent checking the receipt against the quoted label would not find it on a detached HEAD.
fix: Document it: add "`--local` on the PR branch itself also leaves untracked files out" to the `--local` sentence.
Or pass `untracked=not args.local or on-PR-branch` so `--local` changes nothing on the PR branch.
Replace with: (``local checkout `<branch>` `` for a `--local` capture off the PR branch, `local detached checkout` on a detached HEAD).

minor.name: Unused **kwargs on TestCaptureForcedLocal._capture
minor.summary: `_capture` accepts and forwards `**kwargs`, but every caller passes only (script, clone, head); the two tests that need a different flag set call script.capture_pr directly. The parameter is dead.
fix: Drop `**kwargs: object` from the signature and the call, or route the two direct capture_pr calls (lines 417-419, 464-466) through `_capture` with overrides so the parameter earns its place.

minor.name: Forced-vs-default equality holds only because the fixture has no untracked file
minor.summary:
test_on_the_pr_branch_matches_the_default asserts `forced == default` and its name says that `--local` on the PR branch matches the default capture. That is not generally true: `_capture` passes untracked=False (as `_cmd_capture` does for --local, pr_sum.py:384) while the default keeps untracked files (pr_capture.py:195). The two only compare equal because pr_repo carries no untracked file. A reader of the test, or a later change that seeds an untracked file in _build_pr, gets a false contract.

Also (tests): Both captures in test_on_the_pr_branch_matches_the_default leave `today` unset, so PrFacts.date comes from two separate date.today() calls (pr_capture.py:230); a run that crosses midnight between them fails `forced == default`. test_fetch_matches_local_capture avoids this by comparing selected fields.
fix: Rename the test to say what it shows (for example test_on_the_pr_branch_without_untracked_files_matches_the_default), or
Write an untracked file (e.g. src/pkg/new.py) before the two captures and assert the forced capture lacks it while the default lists it as untracked; compare the remaining fields.
Pass today="2026-10-10" to both captures (self._capture(script, clone, head, today="2026-10-10") and the default capture_pr call).

minor.name: CLI diff of a forced-local skeleton checks only the exit code
minor.summary:
test_local_flag_summarizes_a_checkout_off_the_pr_branch ends with `script.main(["diff", ...]) == 0` and never reads the printed diff, so a diff that prints an empty or wrong body (e.g. includes the untracked src/pkg/new.py, or loses the staged file) still passes. This is the only end-to-end `diff` run over a --local skeleton.

Also (tests): lacks_pr_head treats a PR head missing from the local object store as unknown (git exit 128, pr_capture.py:169-171), so `_local_note` stays silent. test_local_flag_notes_a_head_without_the_pr_head covers present-and-contained and present-and-missing only; a regression that turns exit 128 into a note (or a crash) is not caught.
fix: Add a capsys fixture and assert the output holds the `=== src/pkg/staged.py` header and `+s`, and does not name src/pkg/new.py.
Add a case on a `--no-local` fresh clone (_fresh_clone) with --no-fetch and --local, asserting exit 0 and no `note:` in stdout.
